source.title: Exponentially Many Local Minima in Quantum Neural Networks

record.tranche_reason: The study tests quantum neural networks, while the listed versions concern classical networks or specific classical training methods. Its QNN results do not test those versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own QNN optimization results. It cites classical neural-network findings, including Safran & Shamir (2018), but does not test them. The QNN results are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study proves landscape results and reports optimization experiments for parameterized quantum circuits. None tests the classical network architectures, measures, or comparisons specified by V1–V6. Its discussion of classical spurious minima, including Safran and Shamir, supplies context rather than a test of V2.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors establish worst-case datasets producing exponentially many spurious minima for under-parameterized QNNs satisfying linear independence, show this condition holds with high probability in their random-circuit model, and present simulations suggesting difficulty for gradient-based black-box training. They do not establish that every dataset is hard or rule out efficient non-gradient methods.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments train parameterized quantum circuits using square loss and exact gradients, rather than the classical network recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer (Adam, RMSProp, L-BFGS) and number of parameters; the paper reports different dataset settings for constructed and linearly separable concept experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: On constructed quantum circuit instances, random starts frequently converge to suboptimal minima. Adam, RMSProp and L-BFGS each rarely reach the zero-loss global minimum in the 16-parameter experiment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Constructed under-parameterized quantum circuits can be difficult for common optimizers, with empirical global-minimum success rates decaying exponentially with parameter count.

fits_no_version.finding: For the eight-parameter circuit on encoded linearly separable data, at most 4 of 70 starts reach what the authors identify as global minima. Across the tested sizes, success falls sharply without a clear exponential dependence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under-parameterized quantum circuits can exhibit frequent convergence to suboptimal minima even on encodings of linearly separable classical concepts.

record.problems: The numerical evidence is based on classically simulated QNNs and constructed instances; most convergence outcomes are described qualitatively or displayed in figures rather than given as exact success counts. The natural-data experiments use small parameter counts and 70 random initializations per instance.
record.rows_left_out: Supplementary figure-only convergence distributions for additional parameter counts and noisy-label settings were not extracted as separate rows; the core qualitative findings and the stated 8-parameter count are represented above.

untested.parts: All parts: classical convolutional networks, CIFAR training classification error, random or corrupted labels, and model-size and training-recipe qualifications.
All parts: ReLU teacher-student networks, joint width growth, and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
All parts: depth-related training degradation, identity residual shortcuts, and the stated initialization alternatives.
All parts: activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and trainable depth.
All parts: learning rates relative to initial stability limits, transient loss growth, curvature reduction, and edge-of-stability dynamics.
All parts: batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and the Fixup comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The quantum results do not challenge or limit the scope of the explicitly classical versions. No additional result bearing on V1–V6 requires a missing-row entry.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR training error, corrupted or random labels, and the stated model-size, training-duration, and regularization conditions.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, teacher and student width, and the effect of giving the student extra neurons.
Plain versus residual classical convolutional networks and the stated depth, normalization, and initialization comparisons.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation in classical networks, and the stated depth comparisons.
Learning rates relative to stability limits, curvature changes, and sharpness behavior in classical networks.
Batch normalization comparisons in classical networks and Fixup training without normalization.

rows.subject: 4-parameter construction
rows.operation_detail: Train with RMSProp from uniformly random initial parameters and measure loss at convergence.
rows.value: Converged function values fall into discretized values; the global minimum corresponds to the leftmost bar, and success probability is described as very small.
rows.note: The paper describes the distribution qualitatively; it does not state a numerical success count for this setting.
rows.check: The subject is a quantum circuit, outside all six versions; partial is therefore inapplicable. The reported low success probability is supported by Section 6 and Figure 2.

rows.subject: 16-parameter construction
rows.operation_detail: Train from uniformly random initialization and measure whether the optimizer reaches global minimum loss.
rows.value: The method fails to converge to the global minimum with high probability.
rows.note: The paper gives a qualitative probability description, not the exact success count.
rows.check: Quantum circuit optimization does not measure any listed version. Figure 3 supports frequent failure with Adam across 5000 starts; numbers_found='1/1' is not a reported success count and should be removed.
